lockup.summary: The company, its directors, officers and holders of nearly all its stock agreed not to sell for 180 days after the prospectus date, with some exceptions. The lead banks can allow sales sooner with written consent.

what: Retension is a drug company testing an once-a-day pill, RTN-001, to treat high blood pressure and other heart diseases.
proceeds: It plans to use the money, with its existing cash, to finish its Phase 2b trial (about $18 million) and prepare for a Phase 3 trial (about $10 million). The rest is for general business costs.
risks: The company is young, has lost money since it started, expects more losses, and may never make a profit.
If the company cannot keep going as a business, it may have to sell its assets and investors could lose everything.
It needs a lot more money, and failing to raise it could force cuts or an end to its drug programs.
It must grow its team and operations, and it may struggle to manage that growth.
It depends on its senior managers and scientists, and losing them or failing to hire more would hurt the business.
risks_note: The first 5 risk factors, summarised by AI.
